page: Microsoft Azure D96s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs via hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96s_v7 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and high-throughput execution. The Passmark CPU score, extended instructions test, and encryption test all rank in the top tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 556.8 GB/sec, also placing in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is robust, with read-only small block cached memory bandwidth measured at 7051.06 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 135.88 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the average category, while multi-core stress-ng performance is strong.

The hardware configuration and benchmark profile make the D96s_v7 highly suitable for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, database operations, and static web serving, where it achieved a top-tier throughput of 124.31 GB/sec. It also performs well in Redis SET operations, registering 152.07 million operations per second. While it lacks a dedicated GPU, its support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) enables strong performance in CPU-based LLM prompt processing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384 GB of RAM provides a balanced allocation for consolidated workloads without the overhead of specialized GPU or local storage hardware.
